title: Orders API Database Connection Pool Exhaustion

events.description: Deployed orders-api v2.14.0, including new /orders/history endpoint querying orders table by customer_id without a supporting index.
p95 query latency on orders_db begins climbing from 40ms baseline to 400ms+ for queries touching the orders table.
Alert fired: 'orders_db connection pool utilization > 80%' (warning threshold).
Alert fired: 'orders_db connection pool utilization = 100%, connections queuing' (critical threshold).
orders-api begins returning HTTP 500 errors on checkout and order-history requests due to connection pool timeouts.
PagerDuty escalation triggered to on-call SRE (Priya Nandakumar) for orders-api 5xx error rate SLO burn.
On-call SRE acknowledges page, confirms elevated 500 error rate (approx. 60% of checkout requests), begins triage in #incident-1142.
Incident formally declared as SEV1 due to checkout unavailability for majority of users; Marcus Odeya assigned as Incident Commander.
Public status page updated: 'Investigating - Checkout and order history experiencing errors for a subset of users.'
Database SME (Wei Chen) identifies via slow query log that /orders/history queries are performing full table scans on the orders table.

Confirmed root cause: v2.14.0 deploy introduced a query on orders.customer_id with no supporting index, causing full table scans that hold connections open far longer than normal, exhausting the connection pool under normal traffic.
IC decides on rollback-first strategy: revert orders-api to v2.13.2 rather than attempt a live index build under load.
Rollback of orders-api to v2.13.2 initiated.
Rollback to v2.13.2 completed across all regions.
orders_db connection pool utilization drops from 100% to 45%; query p95 latency returns to ~45ms.
HTTP 500 error rate on checkout and order-history endpoints drops below 1%.
Manual end-to-end checkout test succeeds in staging and production canary; no errors observed over 10 minutes of synthetic traffic.
Status page updated: 'Monitoring - A fix has been applied and services are recovering. We are continuing to monitor.'
Incident declared resolved after 40 minutes of stable error rates and normal connection pool utilization.
Status page updated to 'Resolved'. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-08-06.
